slides.0.title: Ontario Overview
slides.0.subtitle: Niagara Peninsula, Lake Erie North Shore, Prince Edward County and the VQA tiers
slides.1.title: Three viticultural areas
slides.1.highlights.0.title: The three VQA areas
slides.1.highlights.0.content: VQA formally recognises three areas: Niagara Peninsula, Lake Erie North Shore and Prince Edward County; within them are 11 sub-appellations (10 in Niagara plus South Islands in Lake Erie North Shore) (Wikipedia, Wine With Seth)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Ontario's scale
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Ontario has about 17,000 acres (about 6,900 ha) of vines, roughly two-thirds of Canada's acreage, and Wikipedia says it makes about 90% of Canadian icewine. Area and winery counts vary by source and are background only (Wine With Seth, Wikipedia)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Emerging regions
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Beyond the VQA areas are four emerging regions: Norfolk and Haldimand Counties, Central Ontario and Georgian Bay, Near the Shore of Lake Huron, and Eastern Ontario (Wine With Seth)
slides.1.content: Ontario's core is three recognised areas plus a few emerging ones.
slides.2.title: Niagara Peninsula
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Canada's largest area
slides.2.highlights.0.content: The Niagara Peninsula is Canada's largest viticultural area at about 13,600 acres (about 5,500 ha), with over 46 varieties and about 55% of Ontario's VQA wineries (VQA Ontario, Wikipedia)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Three physiographic areas
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Niagara has three physiographic areas: the Lake Iroquois Plain, the Niagara Escarpment and the Haldimand Clay Plain; between escarpment and lake are thick clay layers mixed with silt and sand (VQA Ontario)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Less lake influence inland
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Lake effects weaken with distance from the shore, which creates flavour differences between lakeshore and inland sub-appellations; there are also large day–night temperature swings and ample growing-season sunshine (VQA Ontario)
slides.2.content: Niagara is Ontario's centre and Canada's largest area.
slides.3.title: Lake Erie North Shore and Prince Edward County
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Lake Erie North Shore
slides.3.highlights.0.content: At about 42°N it is Ontario's southernmost area with the most heat; Lake Erie is the shallowest and warmest of the Great Lakes. Its one sub-appellation, South Islands, is centred on Pelee Island (Wine With Seth, Wikipedia); elevation is about 172 to 196 m
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Prince Edward County
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Recognised in 2007, it is Ontario's most northerly area and the only one with no sub-appellations; at the eastern end of Lake Ontario, it sits on porous Ordovician limestone with thin clay-loam soils and has the shortest, coolest growing season (Wikipedia, Wine With Seth)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Hilling up
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Winter temperatures in Prince Edward County can fall below -24°C, so growers hill up or bury the vines after harvest to protect the bud wood from lethal freezes (Wine With Seth); Chardonnay and Pinot Noir are the mainstays
slides.3.content: The warmest and the coolest: the two ends of Ontario.
